paper.title: Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit with psi moment condition
unmapped: rewards satisfy a two-sided log-MGF bound by a known convex function psi; the learner uses psi
settings.definition_quote: There exists a convex function $\psi$ on the reals such that, for all $\lambda \geq 0$, $\ln \E\,e^{\lambda (X-\E[X])} \leq \psi(\lambda)$ and $\ln\,\E\,e^{\lambda (\E[X] - X)} \leq \psi(\lambda)$.

simultaneously, the adversary selects a gain vector $g_t=(g_{1,t},\hdots,g_{K,t}) \in [0,1]^K$, possibly with the help of external randomization; the forecaster receives (and observes) the reward $g_{I_t,t}$

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with side information (context set S)
unmapped: finite context set S; context sequence arbitrary but fixed; comparator is best mapping from contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: game rounds $t=1,2,\dots$ are marked by contexts $s_1,s_2,\dots$ from a given context set $\cS$. ... we further assume that the sequence of contexts $s_t$ is arbitrary but fixed.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with expert advice (adversarial contextual bandit, expert case)
unmapped: expert advice may depend on the forecaster's past random plays
settings.definition_quote: at each step $t=1,2,\dots$ the forecaster obtains the expert advice $(\xi_t^1,\dots,\xi_t^N)$, where each $\xi_t^j$ is a probability distribution over arms ... $\ell_t \in [0,1]^K$

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit game with plays drawn from an arbitrary distribution q_t
unmapped: played arm is drawn from an externally chosen distribution q_t with all probabilities >= eps; regret measured for Exp3's own distribution p_t
settings.definition_quote: Consider a $K$-armed bandit game in which at each step $t=1,2,\dots$ the played arm $I_t$ is drawn from an arbitrary distribution $q_t$ over arms. ... $q_{t,i} \ge \ve > 0$

settings.name_in_paper: Competing against the best context set
unmapped: class of context sets {S_theta}; comparator is best (theta, mapping S_theta -> arms)
settings.definition_quote: Consider now a class $\theset{\cS_{\theta}}{\theta\in\Theta}$ of context sets. In this new game, each time step $t$ is marked by the vector $(s_{\theta,t})_{\theta\in\Theta}$ of contexts

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandits with VC policy class
unmapped: policy class F of binary policies with VC dimension d (known to learner); contexts and loss vectors drawn i.i.d. jointly from D
settings.definition_quote: contexts $x_t$ and arm losses $\ell_t$ are realizations of i.i.d. draws from a fixed and unknown distribution $D$ over $\cX \times [0,1]^K$ ... we focus on the case of $K=2$ arms and parametrize classes $\cF$ of policies by their VC-dimension $d$

unmapped: online multiclass classification: learner only observes whether prediction is correct; performance compared with hinge loss of linear classifiers U
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit version, the learner only observes $\ds1_{\yhat_t \neq y_t}$; that is, whether the prediction at time $t$ was correct or not.

settings.name_in_paper: Online linear optimization with bandit feedback, finite action set (bounded scalar loss)
unmapped: learner needs |K| = N and the John's ellipsoid decomposition of conv(K)
settings.definition_quote: we assume that $\cK$ and $\cL$ are such that $|x^{\top} \ell| \leq 1$ for any $(x, \ell) \in \cK \times \cL$. Moreover, we restrict our attention to finite sets $\cK$, with $|\cK| = N$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online combinatorial optimization with semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: learner knows m (size of each action)
settings.definition_quote: the set of arms is $\cC \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$ and the set of linear loss functions is $\cL = [0,1]^d$. We assume $\norm{v}_1 = m$ for all $v\in\cC$ ... after playing $v_t \in \cC$, one observes $(\ell_t(1) v_t(1), \hdots, \ell_t(d) v_t(d))$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online linear optimization with bandit feedback on the Euclidean ball
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cK = \cL = \{x \in \R^d \,:\, \norm{x} \leq 1 \}$ define an online linear optimization problem with bandit feedback.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback
unmapped: r B ⊆ K ⊆ R B; learner knows R (outer radius)
settings.definition_quote: at each time step $t$, the forecaster observes the value of a convex and differentiable loss function $\ell_t$ at the played point $x_t$ and at an extra point $x_t'$ of its choice.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with one-point feedback
unmapped: losses convex, differentiable, uniformly bounded by L (known to learner)
r B ⊆ K ⊆ R B; learner knows R
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cL$ be a set of $G$-Lipschitz differentiable and convex losses, uniformly bounded by $L$

settings.name_in_paper: Nonlinear stochastic bandits (unimodal mean loss on [0,1])
unmapped: mean loss unimodal with unique minimizer
lower growth condition |mu(x)-mu(x')| >= C_L|x-x'| away from x*; learner knows C_L
settings.definition_quote: arms are points in the unit interval $[0,1]$ ... the loss is the realization of an independent random variable $Y_t\in [0,1]$ with expected value $\mu(x_t)$ ... we assume that $\mu$ is unimodal

algorithms.name: OSMD on the Euclidean ball with F(x) = -ln(1-||x||) - ||x||

symbols.psi_star: Legendre-Fenchel transform of the moment function psi

conditions: reward distributions satisfy the psi moment condition (eq:psicond)

source.label: th:ucb
source.quote: Assume that the reward distributions satisfy \eqref{eq:psicond}. Then $(\alpha, \psi)$-UCB with $\alpha > 2$ satisfies $$\oR_n \leq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{\alpha \Delta_i}{\psi^*(\Delta_i / 2)} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)~.$$

results.notes: Survey; algorithm attributed to Auer et al. 2002. Index uses ln t so anytime. is_new set false since survey restates classical result, but no explicit attribution in the statement.

source.label: eq:regretUCBbounded
source.quote: In case of $[0,1]$-valued random variables, taking $\psi(\lambda) = \tfrac{\lambda^2}{8}$ ... gives the following pseudo-regret bound $\oR_n \leq \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{2 \alpha}{\Delta_i} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)$

results.notes: Special case of Theorem th:ucb stated in text (not a separate theorem environment), recorded because the expression differs.

conditions: strategy satisfies E T_i(n) = o(n^a) for every Bernoulli instance, suboptimal arm i and a > 0

source.label: th:LR85
source.quote: Consider a strategy that satisfies $\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions, any arm $i$ with $\Delta_i > 0$, and any $a>0$. Then, for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions the following holds $$\liminf_{n \to +\infty} \frac{\oR_n}{\ln n} \geq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \frac{\Delta_i}{\kl(\mu_i,\mu^*)}~.$$

results.notes: Extracted from Lai & Robbins 1985 (restated in survey); proof given only for two arms.

tuning: eta_t = eta = sqrt(2 ln K/(n K))

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: If Exp3 is run with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln K}{n K}}$, then \oR_n \leq \sqrt{2 n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Losses in [0,1]; pseudo-regret defined with max outside the expectation. Environment set adversarial_adaptive since the setting allows non-oblivious adversaries and pseudo-regret is defined for them; the paper notes pseudo-regret is only meaningful for oblivious adversaries.

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: Moeover, if Exp3 is run with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{t K}}$, then \oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Anytime version.

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: For any given $\delta \in (0,1)$, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K \delta^{-1})}{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K)}{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln(K)}{n}}$ then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K \delta^{-1})}~.

results.notes: Gain version, rewards in [0,1], holds against any adversary.

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: Moreover, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\tfrac{\ln(K)}{n K}}$ while $\eta$ and $\gamma$ are chosen as before, then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln(K)}} \ln(\delta^{-1}) + 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K)}~.

results.notes: Holds for any delta simultaneously (delta not an input).

source.quote: If Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln K }{n}}$ then \E\,R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln K} + \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln K }}~.

results.notes: Obtained by integrating the high-probability bound; valid against non-oblivious adversaries.

symbols.eps_gap: gap parameter of the hard instance: one arm Bernoulli((1+eps)/2), others Bernoulli((1-eps)/2)

conditions: max over the K instances where all arms are Bernoulli((1-eps)/2) except arm i which is Bernoulli((1+eps)/2)

source.label: lem:LBminimax
source.quote: Let $\epsilon \in [0,1)$. For any $i \in \{1,\hdots, K\}$ let $\E_i$ be the expectation against the joint distribution of rewards where all arms are i.i.d. Bernoulli of parameter $\frac{1-\epsilon}{2}$ but arm $i$, which is i.i.d. Bernoulli of parameter $\frac{1+\epsilon}{2}$. Then, for any forecaster, $$\max_{i}  \E_i \sum_{t=1}^n (Y_{i,t} - Y_{I_t,t}) \geq n \epsilon \left(1 - \frac{1}{K} - \sqrt{\epsilon \ln\frac{1+\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}}  \sqrt{\frac{n}{2 K}}\right)$$

results.notes: Lemma used to prove the minimax lower bound; restated from Auer et al. 2002 / Bubeck 2010.

source.label: th:LBminimax
source.quote: Let $\sup$ be the supremum over all distribution of rewards such that, for $i=1,\dots,K$, the rewards $Y_{i,1},Y_{i,2},\ldots\in\{0,1\}$ are i.i.d., and let $\inf$ be the infimum over all forecasters. Then $\inf \sup (\max_{i} \E \sum_{t=1}^n Y_{i,t} - \E \sum_{t=1}^n Y_{I_t,t} ) \geq \frac{1}{20} \sqrt{n K}$

results.notes: Minimax lower bound with stochastic Bernoulli rewards; also implies lower bound for adversarial bandits. Proven in Auer et al. 2002.

tuning: separate Exp3 instance per context, tuned as in eq. (exp3bound)

source.label: th:context-simple
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster for bandits with side information (the $\cS$-Exp3 forecaster, defined in the proof) that satisfies $\oRS_n \le \sqrt{2n |\cS| K\ln K}$ for any set $\cS$ of contexts.

results.notes: M_ctx = |S|. Proof applies the tuned Exp3 bound with n_s per context, which implicitly requires knowing n_s; not discussed in paper. Due to Maillard & Munos 2011.

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: Exp4 without mixing and with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln N}{n K}}$ satisfies \oRx_n \leq \sqrt{2 n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: Recorded exactly as printed. The text and proof (log N/eta + (K/2) sum eta_t) clearly yield sqrt(2 n K ln N); the printed statement appears to swap K and N (typo).

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: On the other hand, with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{t K}}$ it satisfies \oRx_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: As printed; likely typo for 2 sqrt(n K ln N) per the proof.

symbols.eps_q: lower bound on all sampling probabilities q_{t,i}

conditions: q_{t,i} >= eps_q > 0 for all i, t

source.label: th:exp3-rebel
source.quote: If Exp3 without mixing is run with $\tilde{\ell}_{i,t} = \frac{\ell_{i,t}}{q_{i,t}} \ds1_{I_t = i}$ and $\eta_t = \eta = \sqrt{\frac{2\ln K}{n K}}$ then $\max_{k} \E_{I^n \sim q^n} [ \sum_{t=1}^n \E_{i \sim p_t} \ell_{i,t} - \sum_{t=1}^n \ell_{k,t} ] \le \sqrt{\frac{2 n}{\ve}\ln K}$

results.notes: Regret of Exp3's own distribution p_t while arms are sampled from external q_t. Note: with the stated eta, the bound eta n/(2 eps) + ln K/eta does not exactly equal sqrt(2n ln K/eps) unless eps = 1/K; recorded as printed.

source.label: th:exp4-mixing
source.quote: Exp4 with mixing coefficient $\gamma$ and with $\eta_t = \eta = \gamma/K$ satisfies \oRx_n \le \frac{\gamma\,n}{2} + \frac{K\ln N}{\gamma}~.

results.notes: Bound holds for any gamma > 0; horizon marked known since optimising gamma requires n, but bound itself holds for any n.

symbols.S_max: max over theta of |S_theta| (largest context set size)

tuning: gamma of order n^{-1/3}(max|S_theta| K ln K)^{1/3} sqrt(ln|Theta|)

source.label: th:theta-regret
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster achieving $\oR^{\Theta}_n = \mathcal{O}\left(n^{2/3}\left(\max_{\theta\in\Theta}|\cS_{\theta}|K\ln K\right)^{1/3}\sqrt{\ln|\Theta|}\right)$ for any class of context sets.

results.notes: Exp4 with mixing over S-Exp3 experts. Attributed to Maillard & Munos 2011.

symbols.d_VC: VC dimension of the policy class

source.label: eq:vebound
source.quote: For any class $\cF$ of binary policies of VC-dimension $d$ and for all $n > d$, the forecaster VE run with $n' = \sqrt{n(2d\ln\frac{en}{d}+ \ln\frac{3}{\delta})}$ satisfies $\sum_{t=1}^n \ell_{I_t,t} - n\inf_{f\in\cF}\ell_D(f) \leq c\sqrt{n(d\ln\frac{en}{d} + \ln\frac{3}{\delta})}$ for some constant $c > 0$ and with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Regret vs n times the risk of best policy. Compute marked exponential since Exp4.P runs over the projected class F' of size up to (en/d)^d; not explicitly stated. From Beygelzimer et al. 2011.

symbols.U_norm: Frobenius norm of comparator matrix U

conditions: |x^T l| <= 1 for all x in K, l in L

source.label: th:exp2john
source.quote: For any $\eta,\gamma > 0$ such that ${\eta d} \le {\gamma}$, Exp2 with John's exploration satisfies $\oR_n \leq 2 \gamma n + \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \eta n d$. In particular, with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{3 n d}}$ and $\gamma = \eta d$, $\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{3 n d \ln N}$.

results.notes: General bound 2 gamma n + ln N/eta + eta n d for eta d <= gamma also stated. Compute: runs exponential weights over all N actions (polynomial in N, exponential in d for discretizations); marked exponential tentatively. From Bubeck, Cesa-Bianchi, Kakade 2012.

source.label: th:osmdnegent
source.quote: For any set $\cC\subseteq\{0,1\}^d$, if OSMD is run on $\cK=\conv(\cC)$ with $F(x) = \sum_{i=1}^d x_i \ln x_i - \sum_{i=1}^d x_i$ ... In particular, with the estimate \eqref{eq:semibanditestimate} and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2m}{nd}\ln\frac{d}{m}}$, $\oR_n \leq  \sqrt{2 m d n \ln \frac{d}{m}}$.

results.notes: Generic bound (m/eta) ln(d/m) + (eta/2) sum E[x_t(i) l_t(i)^2] also stated. Projection step may be computationally hard. From Audibert, Bubeck, Lugosi 2011.

symbols.q_pot: exponent q > 1 of the potential psi(x) = (-x)^{-q}

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: In particular, choosing the $0$-potential $\psi(x) = (- x)^{-q}$, the estimate~\eqref{eq:semibanditestimate}, and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} \frac{m^{1 - 2/q}}{d^{1 - 2/q}}}$, $\oR_n \leq q \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} m d n}$.

results.notes: Stated eta does not depend on n, which seems to be a typo; recorded as printed. For m=1 gives log-free bound for the adversarial MAB (INF).

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: With $q=2$ this gives $\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{2 m d n}$.

results.notes: q=2 specialisation; for m=1 this is the INF / Tsallis-type log-free bound 2 sqrt(2 K n).

source.label: th:two-point
source.quote: Let $\cK\subseteq\R^d$ be a closed convex set such that $r\,\Ball\subseteq\cK\subseteq R\,\Ball$ for some $r,R > 0$. Let $\cL$ be a set of $G$-Lipschitz differentiable and convex losses. ... Then the following holds $\oR_n \le \frac{R^2}{\eta} + \eta (Gd)^2 n + \delta\left(3 + \frac{R}{r} \right) G n$.

results.notes: G mapped to L_lip; r to r_K.

source.label: th:two-point
source.quote: Moreover, if $\eta = \tfrac{R}{GD\sqrt{n}}$ then for $\delta\to 0$ we have that $\oR_n \le 2RGd\sqrt{n}$.

results.notes: Printed eta uses 'GD', interpreted as G d.

source.number: Theorem (Regret of OSGD with one-point feedback)
source.quote: Then the following holds $\oR_n \le \frac{R^2}{\eta} + \frac{(dL)^2}{\delta^2}\eta n + \delta(3 + \frac{R}{r}) G n$. Moreover, if $\delta = ...$ and $\eta = ...$ then $\oR_n \le 4 n^{3/4}\sqrt{RdL(3 + \tfrac{R}{r})G}$.

source.quote: For any unimodal and $C_H$-Lipschitz mean loss function $\mu : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ that satisfies~(\ref{eq:strongmax}), if the SGS algorithm is run with $\ve_s = C_L\varphi^{-(s+3)}$ then $\oR_n \le \frac{C_H}{C_L^2}8\varphi^6\ln(6n) [ \frac{2\varphi}{\varphi-1}\sqrt{1 + C_L^2 n} + \frac{1}{4}\log_{\phi}^2(1 + C_L^2 n) ]$.
